root_idea.summary: The root centers on intense thirst and the disordered wandering associated with it.
root_idea.development: From thirst come terms for thirst-stricken camels, thirst disease, and water-absorbing or dry sand. The image also extends figuratively to aimless wandering, amorous bewilderment, and passionate love.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form هَامَ rather than the Quranic imperfect surface identity.
Displayed under the supported plural lexical citation form هِيمٌ.

senses.definition: To wander or range without a fixed aim.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression, the wandering is figurative: the poets range through every valley, moving extravagantly among different kinds of speech and exceeding bounds in praise and blame.
A plural noun for camels suffering intense thirst; in the Quran it occurs in the genitive phrase describing drinking like the hīm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bewilderment or distraction arising from amorous desire, including heedless or aimless conduct caused by it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The state may be likened to an affection resembling insanity; the associated course is described as random or without consideration or a definite aim.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who loves intensely or passionately; also a heart characterized by such love.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an intensely loving person and, by extension, to the person's heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intense thirst or the state of suffering severe thirst.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited usage applies هَيْمَانٌ and هَائِمٌ to one suffering severe thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease brought on by thirst, especially a thirst-related disorder of camels that causes them to wander.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical description concerns camels affected by thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become intensely enamored or passionately in love.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a classical use of the verb distinct from its Quranic wandering construction.
A classical verbal use expressing entry into a state of thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sands that absorb or swallow water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate classical nominal use applied to sand with this water-absorbing property.
The term is applied to sand described as dry, by comparison with something suffering thirst.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer to an illustrative poetic example, without a lexical definition.
Covers amorous bewilderment and heedless, aimless conduct.
Covers the affection likened to insanity arising from amorous desire.
Covers intense love in a person and in the heart.
Covers the thirsty-camel meaning and its plural هِيمٌ, with the cited Quranic occurrence.

cautions: هِيمٌ in 56:55 is the plural camel term; related root forms also denote intense thirst, sand, and amorous bewilderment, so those lexical branches are kept separate.
A historical citation convention associated with the camel meaning is not treated as a modern verse locator; the displayed 56:55 location is the independently supplied Quran location.
